This is the default configuration for Tiny Tapeout projects. It should fit most designs.
If you change it, please make sure you understand what you are doing. We are not responsible
if your project fails because of a bad configuration.
!!! DO NOT EDIT THIS FILE unless you know what you are doing !!!
If you get stuck with this config, please open an issue or get in touch via the discord.
Here are some of the variables you may want to change:
PL_TARGET_DENSITY_PCT - You can increase this if Global Placement fails with error GPL-0302.
Users have reported that values up to 80 worked well for them.
CLOCK_PERIOD - Increase this in case you are getting setup time violations.
The value is in nanoseconds, so 20ns == 50MHz.
Hold slack margin - Increase them in case you are getting hold violations.
RUN_LINTER, LINTER_INCLUDE_PDK_MODELS - Disabling the linter is not recommended!
If you need a custom clock configuration, read the following documentation first:
https://tinytapeout.com/faq/#how-can-i-map-an-additional-external-clock-to-one-of-the-gpios
WARP (DECISIONS D-019): the fabric macro warp_tiny (macro/warp_tiny/, 357.12 x 483.84 um).
Placed at the east side, centred vertically: its 152 west-face pins (FrameData, west IO) and
67 south-face pins (FrameStrobe, clock/reset) face open core (BUGS #9). x = 11.52 + 8 x 109.92
(power columns under the chip stripes, D-017) = 1856 x 0.48; y = 270 x 0.42 = 30 rows.
Its nl is the port-only black box src/warp_tiny.v (not in info.yaml source_files), as the
R3 SRAM spike did: synthesis and STA see only its pins (D-019 revision 2).
No '//' keys inside MACROS: LibreLane rejects unknown keys in a Macro (BUGS #10).
WARP (D-019): the macro power grid script from the TRIPWIRE R3 spike (src/pdn_cfg.tcl header).
WARP (D-019 rev 2), settings the R3 SRAM spike needed for a macro on CMOS5L:
cap detailed-routing iterations so a run that cannot converge fails in minutes, not hours
Magic reads standard cells from the PDK, not from the macro GDS
Magic's CMOS5L deck reports false errors inside macros; the precheck's KLayout DRC is sign-off
chip Metal4 stripes cross the macro's Metal4 obstruction over its power columns
LVS treats the fabric macro as a black box
